comments.author: lukifer
comments.why_zh: 有说服力地论证了默认不可变
comments.quote_zh: 让我接受这个想法的是 Rich Hickey 的演讲
comments.text_zh: 不可变性最近相当热门，尽管仍存有争议。有几种流行语言鼓励甚至强制不可变性（Elixir、Clojure）。让我接受这个想法的是 Rich Hickey 的演讲 "The Value of Values"：[VIDEO] 我主要把它看作一张安全网：我更愿意默认使用 const，除非我有充分的理由需要让变量可变。（反过来问：默认可变到底解决了什么问题？）十次里有九次，在函数的整个生命周期里我都不需要改变那个值；而且就算需要改，用不可变的模式（比如用 `const foo = bar.map()` 而不是 `for(x in bar) foo.push()`）往往代码还更干净。得益于 Merkle trees 的魔力，我们通常可以创建新的指针，而不会带来多少内存开销。
comments.text: Immutability has been pretty hot of late, though still controversial. There are several popular languages which encourage or even force immutability (Elixir, Clojure). What sold me on the idea was Rich Hickey's talk, "The Value of Values": [VIDEO] I look at it as mostly a safety net: I'd rather use const by default, unless I have a good reason to be able to mutate the variable. (To flip it around: what problem does being mutable-by-default solve?) 9 times out of 10, I don't need to change the value for the lifecycle of the function; and often if I do, the code is cleaner anyway if I use an immutable pattern (such as `const foo = bar.map()` rather than `for(x in bar) foo.push()`). Thanks to the magic of Merkle trees, we can generally make fresh pointers without it costing much memory overhead.

comments.author: josephg
comments.story_title: The database I wish I had
comments.why_zh: Place 与 Value 之别，以及默认保存完整历史
comments.quote_zh: 很值得一看，尤其是如果你不同意的话
comments.text_zh: 大多数软件都不是 FAANG 那种规模。在数据库大小的长尾里，我猜 95%+ 的数据库都小于几百兆。在这个量级上，存储很便宜，完整保存变更的历史记录绝对应该是默认做法。Rich Hickey 几年前有个很好的演讲，讲 Place 和 Value 的区别。他说会计行业几百年前就在记账里学到了这一课。相对于我们磁盘的容量，用户产生的数据其实并不多。很值得一看，尤其是如果你不同意的话：[VIDEO]
comments.text: Most software isn’t FAANG. In the long tail of database size, I’d guess 95%+ of databases are smaller than a few hundred megs. And at that size, storage is cheap and storing a full historical record of changes should absolutely be the default. Rich Hickey has a great talk on this a few years ago talking about the difference between Place and Value. He says accountants learned this lesson hundreds of years ago with bookkeeping. Users just don’t generate much data relative to the size of our disks. Well worth a watch, especially if you disagree: [VIDEO]

comments.story_title: Programming languages and Frameworks to learn in 2015
comments.why_zh: 对函数式编程重要概念的概述
comments.quote_zh: 也很好，概述了一些对函数式编程很重要的概念
comments.text_zh: 如果你对并发问题有那么一丁点兴趣，就该去研究 Erlang 和 Clojure。摩尔定律基本已经失效了，如今我们靠给每台服务器塞更多 CPU（而不是让单个 CPU 更快）来提升速度，所以并发在编程中越来越无法回避。Joe Armstrong（Erlang）和 Rich Hickey（Clojure）都花了大量时间思考如何在编程语言层面支持并发。Armstrong 讲了一种他称之为“面向并发的编程”的范式。Armstrong 的论文意外地好读，我推荐一读：[LINK] Rich Hickey 的视频演讲“The value of values”也很好，概述了一些对函数式编程很重要的概念：[VIDEO]
comments.text: If you have the slightest interest in the issue of concurrency then you should study Erlang and Clojure. Since Moore's Law has largely faded, and we now gain speed by putting more CPUs in each server (rather than having the individual CPUs be faster) concurrency is an increasingly unavoidable aspect of programming. Joe Armstrong (Erlang) and Rich Hickey (Clojure) have both spent an enormous amount of time thinking about how to support concurrency in a programming language. Armstrong talks about a paradigm that he calls "Concurrency Oriented Programming". Armstrong's thesis is surprisingly readable and I recommend it: [LINK] Rich Hickey's video presentation "The value of values" is also a good overview of some concepts that are important to Functional Programming: [VIDEO]

comments.author: dmitry-vsl
comments.story_title: Show HN: Leporello.js – interactive functional programming IDE for JavaScript
comments.why_zh: 函数式编程中 immutability 的优势
comments.quote_zh: 你可以看看 Rich Hickey 那场富有洞见的演讲 [0]，他在其中讨论了函数式编程中 immutability 的优势。
comments.text_zh: Leporello.js 采用一种务实的函数式方法。你可以像平常那样使用 IO 函数并抛出异常，不需要 IO monad 或 Option monad。然而，有一个关键限制——你不能修改自己的数据结构。不允许修改，因为那会让 time-travel debugging 无法实现。例如，下面的代码是被禁止的：const point = {x: 1, y: 2} point.x = 2 而你应该改用这个：const point = {x: 1, y: 2} const another_point = {...point, x : 2} 在 Leporello.js 中，避免修改数据结构至关重要；你要创建新的数据结构。你可以看看 Rich Hickey 那场富有洞见的演讲 [0]，他在其中讨论了函数式编程中 immutability 的优势。在许多方面，Leporello.js 与 Clojure 很相似。Clojure 是 Leporello.js 的灵感来源，以至于我甚至考虑过先为 Clojure 构建 Leporello.js。[0] [VIDEO]
comments.text: Leporello.js follows a pragmatic functional approach. You can use IO functions and throw exceptions as you typically would, without the need for an IO monad or an Option monad. However, there is one critical limitation – you cannot mutate your data structures. Mutations are not allowed because they would make time-travel debugging impossible. For instance, the following code is forbidden: const point = {x: 1, y: 2} point.x = 2 And instead you should use this: const point = {x: 1, y: 2} const another_point = {...point, x : 2} In Leporello.js, it's vital to avoid mutating data structures; instead, you create new ones. You can watch Rich Hickey's insightful talk [0], where he discusses the advantages of immutability in functional programming. In many ways, Leporello.js bears a resemblance to Clojure. Clojure served as a source of inspiration for Leporello.js, to the extent that I even contemplated building Leporello.js for Clojure first. [0] [VIDEO]

comments.author: slifin
comments.story_title: Write Code Like You Write a Recipe
comments.text_zh: 谁知道 bowl.stir() 到底对 bowl 的内部状态做了什么，以及在此之前得先跑过哪些方法才能达到那个状态——这个 bowl 到底准备好被搅拌了吗？为了到那一步又该先运行哪些方法？文章里的代码有太多都靠好的命名撑着。我倾向于拿宝可梦的喷火龙卡来类比这件事。背景是这样：我有一张这样的卡，而且我对它被弄坏很敏感，所以在这个面向对象的例子里，我把卡放进一个盒子里，只允许你以非常受限的方式与它交互——你不能用你习惯的任何东西去碰它，比如你自己的手套、手等等，只能用我提供的“方法”。所以我可能给你开个小孔让你看它，但你仍然可能透过孔把它弄坏，于是我要写一堆逻辑来确保你不会以错误的方式戳它。希望你我两侧的这些啰嗦是值得的、没有 bug、也没有漏掉情况，希望我开的孔正好在你需要的位置上。显然我不能在盒子上开太多孔，否则盒子还有什么意义？我需要这个盒子来维持我的理智。另一种选择是我直接把卡给你，承担你可能把它弄坏的风险——这对我的身心健康是场灾难。或者我把卡完美复制一份，把副本给你，那样副本怎样我都无所谓，在我看来这要容易得多。所以拜托：别再给别的开发者造那种要透过小孔偷看的鬼畜盒子了，直接选一门能高效实现不可变性的语言吧。
comments.text: Who knows what bowl.stir() actually does to the internal state of bowl, and what methods should have been run up until this point to get into that state, is the bowl ready to stir? What methods should have already run for that? So much of the article's code is crutched on good naming I like to think of this in terms of the Charizard Pokemon card For context in this example I have this card and I'm sensitive about damage to it so in this OO example I put the card in a box and allow you to interact with it in a very limited way, you cannot use anything you're used to to interact with it like your own gloves or hands etc Just my "methods" so I might give you a tiny hole to look at it, you could still damage it through the hole, so I have lots of logic to ensure you cannot poke it incorrectly hopefully the verbosity on both your and my side is/was worth it and bug free and not missing cases, hopefully my hole was in the right place for your uses Obviously I can't give you too many holes in the box otherwise what's the point in the box? I need the box to maintain my sanity The other alternative is I just give you the card, and take the risk that you might damage it, this is a disaster for my well being OR I duplicate the card perfectly and give you the duplicate in which case I don't care what happens to the duplicate, MUCH easier in my opinion, so please Stop creating hellish boxes with holes for other developers to peak through just choose a language with efficient immutability
